claim_verdicts.evidence: "Kubeadm is a tool built to provide `kubeadm init` and `kubeadm join` as best-practice \"fast paths\" for creating Kubernetes clusters." kubeadm init workflow: generates CA, kubeconfigs, static Pod manifests for the control plane on the node where it runs. (refs mirror is the v1.37 site; page content is long-standing.)

"By design, it cares only about bootstrapping, not about provisioning machines." "kubeadm **will not** install or manage `kubelet` or `kubectl` for you". "If multiple or no container runtimes are detected kubeadm will throw an error". "The kubelet is now restarting every few seconds, as it waits in a crashloop for kubeadm to tell it what to do." Round 2: lesson now says 'runtime running, kubelet installed' in s3, s4, s6, s9.

claim_verdicts.evidence: "You must deploy a Container Network Interface (CNI) based Pod network add-on... Cluster DNS (CoreDNS) will not start up before a network is installed." Troubleshooting: "kubeadm is network provider-agnostic, so the admin should install the pod network add-on of choice". DaemonSet: "the node is not marked as ready because the network plugin is not running there".

kind Configuration: "KIND uses kubeadm to configure cluster nodes." "Formally KIND runs `kubeadm init` on the first control-plane node" "On every additional node ... worker or control-plane (in HA mode), KIND runs `kubeadm join`". Initial design: "Once kubeadm has booted, we export the KUBECONFIG, then apply an overlay network." Capture: grep of /kind/kubeadm.conf -> 'kind: ClusterConfiguration'.

Capture: 'v1.34.11', then 'active' twice for `systemctl is-active kubelet containerd`. version-skew.txt at stage-3: RUNTIME 'containerd://2.3.4' on all three nodes. Round 2: lesson s5 now says 'are installed and running on the node' (run-time state), matching the capture.

"Generates a self-signed CA to set up identities for each component in the cluster... (`/etc/kubernetes/pki` by default)." "Writes kubeconfig files in `/etc/kubernetes/` for the kubelet, the controller-manager, and the scheduler ... each with its own identity". Round 2: ledger and s4 now say most certs sit in pki, the scheduler's and controller manager's in kubeconfig files in /etc/kubernetes.

"Generates static Pod manifests for the API server, controller-manager and scheduler. In case an external etcd is not provided, an additional static Pod manifest is generated for etcd. Static Pod manifests are written to `/etc/kubernetes/manifests`; the kubelet watches this directory for Pods to create on startup." Capture lists the four files.

"_Static Pods_ are managed directly by the kubelet daemon on a specific node, without the API server observing them." "the kubelet directly supervises each static Pod (and restarts it if it fails)." "The main use for static Pods is to run a self-hosted control plane".

"The kubelet automatically tries to create a mirror Pod on the Kubernetes API server for each static Pod... visible on the API server, but cannot be controlled from there. The Pod names will be suffixed with the node hostname with a leading hyphen." "kubeadm uses static Pods to run kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, and etcd".

Components: "kube-controller-manager: Runs controllers to implement Kubernetes API behavior." Glossary: "Control plane component that runs controller processes... they are all compiled into a single binary and run in a single process."

Required CAs: "ca.crt,key | kubernetes-ca | Kubernetes general CA", "etcd/ca.crt,key | etcd-ca | For all etcd-related functions", "front-proxy-ca.crt,key | ... For the front-end proxy". "it is also necessary to get a public/private key pair for service account management, `sa.key` and `sa.pub`." "kube-apiserver | apiserver.key | apiserver.crt"; "apiserver-etcd-client.crt | --etcd-certfile".

Table: "etcd-ca | etcd/ca.key | etcd/ca.crt | etcd | | --trusted-ca-file,--peer-trusted-ca-file". etcd task: with --client-cert-auth "it verifies the certificates from clients by using system CAs or the CA passed in by `--trusted-ca-file`". Round 2: ledger and s5 now use the round-1 suggested_text ('checks client certificates against etcd/ca'), no 'only'.

v1.34 page: "Client certificates generated by kubeadm expire after 1 year." "certificateValidityPeriod: 8760h # Default: 365 days × 24 hours = 1 year" "caCertificateValidityPeriod: 87600h # Default: 365 days × 24 hours * 10 = 10 years". Same text in refs (v1.37) L13, L73-74.

Docs sample output: certificate rows 'RESIDUAL TIME 364d', CA rows '9y'. "The command shows expiration/residual time for the client certificates in the /etc/kubernetes/pki folder and for the client certificate embedded in the kubeconfig files used by kubeadm (admin.conf, controller-manager.conf and scheduler.conf)." Capture header and rows match the format (dates masked).

"`kubeadm upgrade` also automatically renews the certificates that it manages on this node. To opt-out ... `--certificate-renewal=false`". "if you ... perform Kubernetes version upgrades regularly (less than 1 year in between each upgrade), kubeadm will take care of keeping your cluster up to date". Round 2: s5, s6 bullet 3, summary 5 and q4 explanation now carry 'by default' and 'on each node it upgrades'.

issues.quote: kubeadm is not the only way to build a cluster on your own machines.
issues.text: Carried from round 1. Section 5 is long: two code blocks, a long capture, then paragraphs on static Pods, authorities, expiry, and finally an alternative to kubeadm that is unrelated to the code. The last paragraph still feels like a different lesson tacked on.
issues.fix: Move the 'kubeadm is not the only way…' paragraph to the end of section 4, after the paragraph about what kubeadm does not install, or shorten it to two sentences if section 4 has no room.

issues.quote: Some distributions of Kubernetes, packages that install Kubernetes and its parts as one program, made for small machines bundle the container runtime, the control-plane components and a network plugin into one install.
issues.text: New in the changed part. The added clause sits between 'distributions of Kubernetes' and 'made for small machines', so I lost the subject and had to re-read twice to find the verb 'bundle'.
issues.fix: Split into two sentences: 'Some distributions of Kubernetes are made for small machines. A distribution is a package that installs Kubernetes and its parts as one program; these bundle the container runtime, the control-plane components and a network plugin into one install.'
